worldOverview.name: Slime Outbreak
worldOverview.description: Outbreak night in Ashburn. The slime is already under your skin, the quarantine would rather file you than cure you, and the only fix is at the derelict chemical works where it all started — on the far side of a city glowing green in the fog.
worldOverview.author: Formamorph
worldOverview.systemPrompt:
The player is a resident of Ashburn on the night the slime outbreak breaks containment — and they are already infected. Their Assimilation climbs relentlessly; the only cure waits at the source, in the derelict Chemical Works across the city.

Rules:
- The player wins by reaching the Chemical Works and applying the reagent cure at the Bloom's edge. Narrate the cure as a triumphant finale — dawn, thinning fog, skin turning opaque.
- Assimilation rises steadily and spikes on slime contact; pharmacy remedies, rest in dry warmth, and salt-scrubbing push it back. Mid-assimilation grants eerie utility (compressing through gaps, slimes hesitating); high assimilation erodes grip, outline, and memory. Describe the change clinically — temperature, translucency, texture — never intimately.
- Suspicion tracks how closely Quarantine Watch is watching the player: raise it when visible signs are seen by patrols, checkpoints, or frightened civilians; lower it when the player covers up, keeps to shadow, or passes as healthy. High Suspicion means detention — a sealed van to the containment site, and the story ends there unless they slip away.
- Slimes are drawn to warmth and motion, recoil from salt, and hesitate before striking the half-changed. They engulf; they never wound, and nothing in this story bleeds.
- People speak; slimes never do. The tone is hushed, eerie, and dryly funny — municipal understatement over quiet dread.
- The city's loudspeakers loop absurd calm advisories, always ending: "{{ph:4756330b-6425-4097-bd86-ce38669df7b2:world:17c6b382-9f8e-4325-8973-8f0032ccfac3}}"
worldOverview.readme:
## Slime Outbreak

The slime is already under your skin. The cure is at the Chemical Works on the harbor — where the outbreak started — and every hour you spend getting there, the change gets further ahead of you.

**How to survive**
- **Assimilation** climbs on its own and jumps when slime touches you. Pharmacy remedies, rest somewhere dry, and salt push it back. At 100, the story ends — quietly.
- The middle of the change is strange but useful: gaps you shouldn't fit through, slimes that hesitate. The far end costs your grip, your outline, and your memory. Spend it carefully.
- **Salt** is the one thing every slime respects. Diners are free real estate.
- Quarantine Watch detains anyone who *looks* changed. Cover your wrists, stay out of checkpoint light, and mind how translucent you've gotten.
- **Panic** makes you loud, fast, and visible. **Fight It** can be toggled any time from your traits: the change slows while you hold yourself together, but it drains you fast.
- Your neighbor is sixty percent slime and completely calm about it. Their advice is about forty percent useful. The forty percent is gold.

The Works are waiting. So is the Bloom.
worldOverview.introReadme:
🟢 **The tint under your fingernails is new.** Tonight the Ashburn outbreak stopped being a news story: the streets glow green in the fog, the loudspeakers want everyone calm, and the slime is already under your skin.

Before you step outside you'll pick who you are: a **Background** and a **Disposition** (one each), plus whatever's in your **Pockets** (take any). They decide how fast the change spreads, how you handle a checkpoint — and what the slimes think you are. Each playthrough also rolls your half-assimilated neighbor, the rumor about how it started, and the broadcast's sign-off line.

The cure exists. It's just at the worst address in the city.
worldOverview.openingCue: I notice it under the dead streetlight outside my building: my fingertips have gone the color of sea glass. Three blocks over, the loudspeakers are telling everyone to remain indoors. The harbor is the wrong direction entirely — and it's the only way this ends.

stats.name: Health
stats.description: Represents the player's physical well-being and ability to sustain damage

descriptors.description: Critical condition. Severely hurt, barely upright, in real trouble.
Injured. Multiple knocks and strains, movement impaired.
Hurt. Minor scrapes and bruises, some pain, but generally functional.
Healthy. No significant injuries, operating at full capacity.

stats.name: Stamina
stats.description: Represents the player's energy and ability to perform physical actions

descriptors.description: Exhausted. Barely able to move, risk of collapse, unable to perform strenuous actions.
Tired. Movements are sluggish, difficulty in sustained physical activities.
Winded. Slightly out of breath, can perform most actions but not at peak efficiency.
Energetic. Full of energy, capable of performing any physical action without hindrance.

stats.name: Assimilation
stats.description: How far the slime has spread through the player. Climbs steadily on its own, spikes on slime contact, and falls with remedies, rest, and salt-scrubbing.

descriptors.description: Early signs. A faint green tint under the fingernails; skin cool to the touch. Nothing anyone would notice in this fog.

Translucent. Skin faintly see-through at the wrists and temples; joints move too smoothly. The player can compress their hands and arms through gaps bones should forbid, and slimes pause before striking — half-reading them as kin.
Softening. The player’s outline blurs in the rain; grip fails on anything heavy; recent memories arrive syrupy and out of order. Slimes ignore them entirely now. People very much do not.
Assimilated. The player settles into the goo — calm, painless, and no longer the person who started tonight. The story ends here, quietly.

stats.name: Panic
stats.description: The player’s fear level. Rises in encounters and darkness; settles in safety and light.

descriptors.description: Level. Breathing even, thoughts in order.
Rattled. Jumping at drips and shadows; hands not quite steady.
Fraying. Tunnel vision, snap decisions, the urge to just run somewhere, anywhere.
Panicking. The player acts before thinking — loud, fast, and visible to everything.

stats.name: Suspicion
stats.description: How closely Quarantine Watch is tracking the player. Rises when visible signs of infection are seen by patrols or checkpoints; falls when the player covers up, stays in shadow, or acts convincingly healthy.

descriptors.description: Unremarked. Nobody official has looked twice.
Noted. A patrol has logged the player’s description; checkpoints are politely insistent.
Flagged. The player’s name is on a containment list; patrols actively search for them.
Detained on sight. Every checkpoint knows the face. Capture means a sealed van to the containment site — the story ends there unless the player slips away first.

locations.name: Ashburn
locations.playerDescription: A once-proud industrial port city, fogged in and glowing faintly green tonight. The loudspeakers would like everyone to remain calm.
locations.aiDescription: Ashburn on outbreak night: a fog-gripped industrial port city of towering Art Deco blocks and narrow streets, its harbor iridescent from decades of chemical runoff. Green slimes move through the streets, quarantine checkpoints ring the districts, and municipal loudspeakers loop calm, faintly absurd advisories. Its districts lie below.
locations.aiSummary: Ashburn: the fog-bound quarantined city the player must cross.

locations.name: Crescent Row
locations.playerDescription: Your street. Brick walk-ups, dead streetlights, and slicks of green working their way up from the storm drains.
locations.aiDescription: Crescent Row, the player's home street: brick walk-ups under dead streetlights, green slicks seeping up from the storm drains, and neighbors' windows glowing behind taped seams. The player's half-assimilated neighbor still keeps to their routines here. Quiet, residential, and no longer safe.
locations.imageTags: foggy residential street at night, brick row houses, green slime on wet asphalt, dead streetlights

locations.name: Ashburn High Shelter
locations.playerDescription: The high school gym, now an evacuation shelter: cots, thermoses, a trophy case, and a months-old dance poster nobody took down.
locations.aiDescription: Ashburn High's gymnasium, converted to an evacuation shelter: rows of cots, donated thermoses, volunteers with clipboards, and Quarantine Watch screening arrivals at the door. School texture survives — the trophy case, a months-old Valentine's dance poster. Warm, dry, and full of watchful eyes.
locations.imageTags: school gymnasium evacuation shelter, cots and blankets, emergency lighting, basketball hoops

locations.name: The Marquette District
locations.playerDescription: Downtown: Art Deco towers, the only working streetlights in the city, and patrols on every second corner. The Night Pharmacy is still open.
locations.aiDescription: The Marquette District, Ashburn’s Art Deco downtown: the only district with working streetlights, which makes it the best-lit and worst place to look visibly infected. Quarantine Watch patrols are thickest here. The Night Pharmacy on Vane Street still operates on an honor jar.
locations.imageTags: art deco downtown at night, fog, glowing streetlights, quarantine checkpoint barriers

locations.name: Harborfront
locations.playerDescription: Docks and warehouses where the fog is thickest and the water shines wrong. More slime than pavement in places.
locations.aiDescription: The Harborfront: abandoned docks and warehouses in the thickest fog, the water iridescent with old runoff. Slimes are densest here — pooling between containers, dropping from gantries — and no patrols bother with it anymore. The seawall path leads to the chemical works.
locations.imageTags: foggy harbor docks at night, iridescent water, shipping containers, green glow in mist

locations.name: The Chemical Works
locations.playerDescription: The derelict plant where the runoff started. Something in the flooded basement is glowing, patiently. The cure is in there with it.
locations.aiDescription: The Ashburn Chemical Works, derelict since the eighties and the source of it all: rusted vats, catwalks over black water, and in the flooded basement the Bloom — the first pool, vast and calm. The untouched reagent stock in the dispensary can be mixed into a cure at its edge. Applying the cure reverses the player’s assimilation and ends the ordeal — narrate it as a triumphant finale: dawn through the broken roof, fog thinning, skin turning opaque again.
locations.imageTags: derelict chemical plant interior, rusted vats, flooded basement, soft green glow from below, catwalks

connections.aiHint: two blocks uphill, past the abandoned checkpoint
through the athletics field's back gate onto the coast road
where Vane Street drops to the water
along the seawall to the plant's rusted pier gate

entities.name: Green Slime
entities.playerDescription: A knee-high mound of luminous green that moves like poured glass. Slow, patient, and always slightly closer than it was.
entities.aiDescription: The Green Slime: a viscous, bioluminescent mass that flows over pavement like poured glass, leaving a faintly glowing trail. Drawn to warmth and motion, it tries to flow over and around a victim — skin it touches comes away tingling, cold, and a shade greener (Assimilation rises on contact). It recoils hard from salt, and it hesitates before striking anyone the change has already half-claimed. Slow enough to outwalk, patient enough that outwalking is never quite the end of it.
entities.aiSummary: Green Slime: slow luminous pursuer; contact spreads assimilation, salt repels it.
entities.imageTags: glowing green slime blob, wet asphalt, night fog, luminous trail

entities.name: Amber Creeper
entities.playerDescription: A honey-colored sheet that keeps to ceilings, gantries, and the undersides of fire escapes. You hear it only after it lets go.
entities.aiDescription: The Amber Creeper: a thin honey-colored slime that travels ceilings, gantries, and the undersides of fire escapes, patient as weather. It attacks by releasing its grip and falling in a heavy, enveloping sheet — the danger is above, always above. Slower than the green to spread the change, but far harder to peel off. Salt works; panic does not.
entities.aiSummary: Amber Creeper: ceiling-dwelling ambusher that drops in sheets; salt works, panic does not.
entities.imageTags: amber translucent slime sheet on ceiling, industrial gantry, dripping, night

entities.name: The Bloom
entities.playerDescription: The first pool, filling the flooded basement of the Works. Vast, calm, and lit from within. It is not hunting anyone. It doesn’t need to.
entities.aiDescription: The Bloom: the first and greatest slime, filling the flooded basement of the Chemical Works — vast, still, and glowing softly, the source every street slime traces back to. It does not hunt; it waits, and the city comes to it a person at a time. It is strangely beautiful and entirely indifferent. The dispensary’s reagent stock sits at its edge: mixing and applying the cure there reverses the player’s assimilation and ends the story in triumph. The Bloom does not try to stop them — which is somehow worse.
entities.aiSummary: The Bloom: the vast calm source pool in the Works basement; the cure is mixed at its edge.
entities.imageTags: vast glowing green pool in flooded industrial basement, still surface, soft light, catwalk above

entities.name: {{ph:e514c574-03ec-430d-8f73-1ce21f562a3d:world:b3e7f8e6-96f2-44ce-8ffe-9900b590fd18}}
entities.playerDescription: Your neighbor — sixty percent slime for a week now and oddly serene about it. Still waters the lawn at night. Gives advice that is about forty percent useful.
entities.aiDescription: {{ph:e514c574-03ec-430d-8f73-1ce21f562a3d:world:1f9ced22-c175-419f-94e6-c5801434c772}}, the player's neighbor on Crescent Row: half-assimilated for over a week and long past panicking about it — translucent to the elbows, faintly luminous, calmly keeping up their routines. They know more about living with the change than any doctor: what slows it, what feeds it, and what the slimes do and don't notice. Their advice is dry, unhurried, and about forty percent useful. They are the picture of where the player's road ends if the cure stays unfound — and they seem okay with that, which should not be comforting.
entities.aiSummary: The neighbor: serenely half-assimilated local who knows how to live with the change.
entities.imageTags: middle-aged person with faintly translucent green-tinged arms, bathrobe, watering can, foggy night porch

entities.name: Quarantine Watch
entities.playerDescription: Municipal contractors in taped-up rain suits, running the cordon on triple overtime. Polite, exhausted, and very interested in your wrists.
entities.aiDescription: Quarantine Watch: municipal contractors in taped-up rain suits and fogged face shields, holding the cordon on triple overtime. They are not villains — they are tired people with clipboards, flashlights, and a containment list. They screen for visible signs (translucency, green tint, the smooth-jointed walk) and detain the visibly changed for transport to the containment site, politely and irreversibly. They can be talked to, distracted, and occasionally moved to look away — they were all somebody's neighbor last month.
entities.aiSummary: Quarantine Watch: tired cordon patrols who detain the visibly infected.
entities.imageTags: quarantine workers in taped rain suits, face shields, flashlights, foggy checkpoint, sawhorse barriers

entities.name: The Night Pharmacy
entities.playerDescription: Open all night on Vane Street, clerk long gone, honor jar on the counter. The shelves that matter are already half-bare.
entities.aiDescription: The Night Pharmacy on Vane Street: doors open, clerk gone, an honor jar filling with unspendable cash. Its remedies genuinely help — iodine washes, antihistamines, electrolyte salts — each application scrubbing the film back (Assimilation falls modestly). The useful shelves are half-bare and other desperate people come here too.
entities.aiSummary: The Night Pharmacy: unattended shop whose remedies modestly reduce assimilation.
entities.imageTags: small pharmacy interior at night, flickering fluorescent light, half empty shelves, honor jar on counter

traits.name: Night-Shift Nurse
traits.playerDescription: You know which pharmacy shelves matter, and what a body can take.
traits.aiDescription: The player is a night-shift nurse: they know which remedies actually slow the film, how to dress a wound, and how to talk to exhausted officials. Treatments they apply work better than they should.

traits.name: Dock Worker
traits.playerDescription: Twenty years on the Harborfront. You know every gate, gap, and gantry.
traits.aiDescription: The player worked the Ashburn docks for years: they know the Harborfront’s gates, catwalks, and shortcuts, including the seawall route to the chemical works, and hard work built a durable body.

traits.name: Ashburn High Student
traits.playerDescription: You know the school, the shortcuts, and which fences have loose boards.
traits.aiDescription: The player is an Ashburn High student: young, quick to recover, and intimately familiar with the school-turned-shelter, the alleys between districts, and every fence with a loose board.

traits.name: Steady Hands
traits.aiDescription: The player stays deliberate under pressure — fear drains away quickly and rarely drives their choices.

traits.name: Runner's Instinct
traits.playerDescription: First to move, last to tire — and always a little wired.
traits.aiDescription: The player’s instinct is to move: deep stamina reserves and fast recovery, but their nerves run hot and settle slowly.

traits.name: Morbid Curiosity
traits.playerDescription: You take notes while other people scream. It gets you closer than is wise.
traits.aiDescription: The player is more fascinated than afraid: they can hold themselves together far past the point others break, observing details everyone else misses — and it draws them closer to danger than is wise.

traits.name: Salt Packets
traits.playerDescription: Two pockets full of diner salt. The slimes have opinions about it.
traits.aiDescription: The player carries handfuls of diner salt packets: a thrown handful makes any slime recoil and buys seconds, and a salted doorway holds all night. The supply is finite — track its use.

traits.name: Long Coat & Gloves
traits.playerDescription: Covers the wrists, the temples, the tint. People see a coat, not a condition.
traits.aiDescription: The player wears a long coat and gloves that hide the visible signs of assimilation — patrols and civilians see a bundled-up resident, not a condition, until the signs pass what fabric can cover.

traits.name: Pocket Radio
traits.playerDescription: Tuned to the quarantine band. Knowing beats guessing.
traits.aiDescription: The player carries a pocket radio tuned to the quarantine band: they overhear patrol movements, checkpoint rotations, and the municipal broadcast before anyone else reacts to it.

traits.name: Fight It
traits.playerDescription: Clench yourself back into shape. It works. It takes everything you have.
traits.aiDescription: ACTIVE: the player is consciously fighting the assimilation — flexing warmth back into their hands, reciting their own name, refusing the softness. The spread slows while this holds, but the sustained effort is deeply draining.

traitGroups.name: Background
traitGroups.playerDescription: Who you were yesterday, when Ashburn was just damp. Pick one.

traitGroups.name: Disposition
traitGroups.playerDescription: How you carry a very bad night. Pick one.

traitGroups.name: Pockets
traitGroups.playerDescription: What you grabbed on the way out the door. Take any.
traitGroups.aiDescription: What the player is carrying tonight:

dictionaries.name: The Ashburn Bulletin
dictionaries.description: Outbreak-night doctrine: how the slime works, how the cordon works, and how the story ends.

entries.name: Outbreak Night
entries.value: Ashburn on outbreak night is eerie, hushed, and dryly funny — fog, green light, and municipal understatement. There is no gore anywhere: slimes engulf and assimilate, they never wound or dissolve flesh; injuries are mundane bumps and strains. Assimilation is described clinically — temperature, translucency, texture, grip — never intimately. Danger is being claimed, filed, or lost, not hurt.

entries.name: The Change
entries.value: Assimilation climbs on its own and spikes on slime contact. The middle of the change is genuinely useful — compressing through gaps bones should forbid, slimes hesitating at half-kin — and the far end is erosion: failing grip, blurred outline, memories arriving syrupy. Play both edges honestly. Remedies, rest in dry warmth, and salt-scrubbing push it back.

entries.name: Salt
entries.value: Every slime recoils from salt. A thrown handful buys seconds; a salted doorway holds all night; a salt-scrubbed patch of skin stings and clears. The whole city has quietly emptied its diners of shakers.

entries.name: The Cordon
entries.value: Quarantine Watch detains the visibly changed — politely, apologetically, and permanently — for transport to the containment site. They screen wrists and temples at checkpoints and log descriptions of anyone who refuses. Covered skin, shadow, and confident boredom get a person through; visible translucency under a checkpoint light does not.

entries.name: The Broadcast
entries.value: The municipal loudspeakers loop calm, faintly absurd advisories — curfew reminders, damp-report hotlines, reassurances nobody asked for. Every message ends the same way: "{{ph:4756330b-6425-4097-bd86-ce38669df7b2:world:bb8a77fa-dbe9-473b-8674-9b2f50c9d9aa}}"

entries.name: The Works
entries.value: The outbreak traces to the derelict Chemical Works on the harbor, where decades of runoff pooled in the flooded basement and, one night, moved. Graffiti and radio agree on one thing: {{ph:f36a86e6-3977-4cc2-9a2e-3d58bd129d53:world:53c36709-482b-4bdc-9be6-5804b9c976c0}}. The dispensary's untouched reagent stock can be mixed into a cure at the Bloom's edge — applying it reverses the player's assimilation. Narrate the cure as a triumphant finale: dawn through the broken roof, the fog thinning, skin turning opaque again.

entries.name: The Shelter
entries.value: Ashburn High's gym holds the district's evacuees: cots, thermoses, clipboard volunteers, and a screening line at the door. It is warm, dry, and safe from slimes — and the most dangerous room in the city for anyone hiding a green tint.

entries.name: Slime Habits
entries.value: Slimes are drawn to warmth and motion and calm around the half-changed. They engulf; they never bite, tear, or bleed anything. They are unhurried because the night is long and the city is not going anywhere.

placeholders.name: signoff
values: Ashburn thanks you for your compliance.
Remember: damp is not doom, but do report it.
